text: What Time Is It Now, Where You Are?
author: Colum McCann
description: A sentence that opens with a main clause then keeps adding participial and descriptive phrases, so meaning accrues in layers.
tryPrompt: Write one cumulative sentence that opens on a clear image then adds three layers of detail without a full stop.

text: What Time Is It Now, Where You Are?
author: Colum McCann
description: A story about the making of a story, so the act of composition is visible inside the piece.
tryPrompt: Write a short passage where a writer figure shapes the very scene the reader is reading.

text: What Time Is It Now, Where You Are?
author: Colum McCann
description: Addressing a you, which pulls the reader into the frame and blurs writer, character and reader.
tryPrompt: Write an opening in the second person that makes the reader feel implicated in the scene.

text: What Time Is It Now, Where You Are?
author: Colum McCann
description: The narrator steps out to comment on the choices being made, foregrounding craft.
tryPrompt: Write two sentences where the narrator pauses to weigh a choice about how the scene should go.

author: Geraldine Brooks
description: Moving between a personal story and a broader reflection, so the idea is earned through experience.
tryPrompt: Write a short passage that opens on an anecdote then turns to a larger idea it raises.

author: Geraldine Brooks
description: Drawing on other texts and writers to open out the reflection.
tryPrompt: Write a sentence that uses another text or writer to deepen your own point, woven in not dropped in.

author: Geraldine Brooks
description: Ending on a question or an unresolved thought rather than a neat conclusion.
tryPrompt: Write a closing that leaves the idea open without tying it off too neatly.

author: Geraldine Brooks
description: Building enough grounded detail that a broader speculation feels warranted.
tryPrompt: Write a passage that lays down concrete detail then earns a speculative claim from it.

author: Zadie Smith
description: Organising the piece into named or numbered sections that stage the thinking.
tryPrompt: Sketch two short sections with headings that move an idea forward in stages.

author: Zadie Smith
description: Moving between the colloquial and the analytical for effect and control of tone.
tryPrompt: Write a passage that shifts once from a casual register to a precise analytical one.

author: Zadie Smith
description: Carrying one governing metaphor across the piece to hold the ideas together.
tryPrompt: Choose one metaphor for the writing process and extend it across three sentences.

author: Zadie Smith
description: Naming the moves of writing itself, so the reflection on craft is precise.
tryPrompt: Write a sentence that names a specific craft move and what it does, precisely.

author: Unit teaching
description: Opening on a concrete story that grounds and warms the argument before the claim.
tryPrompt: Write an opening anecdote that makes a reader care before you state your stance.

author: Unit teaching
description: Naming the strongest opposing view then answering it, which builds credibility.
tryPrompt: Write a sentence that concedes the best counterargument then turns it to your advantage.
